newsitem.title: USA: US Northeast spot power market soft on mild temps.
newsitem.headline: US Northeast spot power market soft on mild temps.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity market in the U.S. Northeast remained soft on tepid demand linked to a mild weather system lingering over some of the region through the end of the week.
Some regional utilities and generators decided to switch off their more costly generation today, and keep them in so called "reserve shutdown" until power usage picks up, market sources said.
"Units are being taken down. There's excess generation around. You can't give it away," a New York trader said.
By eliminating extra generation capacity, producers were able to keep day-ahead prices from toppling like other regions because of the mild weather, traders said.
"You may find deals on an hourly basis," the trader said.

The latest forecast showed temperatures in southern half of the region would stay well-above normal until the end of the week, while an Arctic system would descend into the northern part of Northeast by midweek, pushing temperatures five to 10 degrees below normal.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices for Tuesday delivery in the western part of the New York Power Pool (NYPP) were assessed near $23.00-$24.00 a megawatt hour (MWh). For export into the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland Interconnect (PJM) district, western NYPP generation was valued at $18.50-$19.50.
Today's quotes compared with Friday's $20.00-$22.00 for Monday delivery.
Day-ahead prices for firm, peak PJM power finished at $17.00-$19.00, down $1.50-$2.00 from Friday's levels.
Off-peak, non-firm power for next-day delivery in western NYPP held in a notional range of $14.00-$15.00.
In eastern NYPP, peak, non-firm power for Tuesday was still pegged at $26.50-$28.00/MWh.
Eastern NYPP electricity for off-peak, non-firm delivery Tuesday remained at $18.00-$19.00.
In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for Tuesday at Northeast Utilities' (NU) border stayed at $30.00-$33.00.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for day-ahead delivery to the NU border was still assessed at $20.00-$22.00.
"You're probably not going to see new prices until the New Year," the trader said.
Mild weather in the Northeast rendered little need for generators to buy swing natural gas for power production, market sources noted.
Swing prices of delivery to the New York City gate were today assessed in at $3.40-$3.50 per million British thermal unit (mmBtu) range, weaker than Friday's quotes mainly in the $3.50 area.
On the New York Mercantile Exchange, February Henry Hub natgas futures continued their Friday plunge, last down 28.9 cents at $2.695.
